    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that cyber criminals are moving away from mass phishing scams and focusing on more targeted attacks, increasingly using trusted websites and services to trick victims, according to a upcoming report from KnowBe4.
    • Sources indicate that the tech giant's Phishing Threat Trends Report, Vol.
    • Rather than sending the same fraudulent message to thousands of people, criminals are spending more time researching their targets and creating convincing messages that appear to come from trusted coworkers, businesses, and technology platforms.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that cyber criminals are moving away from mass phishing scams and focusing on more targeted attacks, increasingly using trusted websites and services to trick victims, according to a upcoming report from KnowBe4. The security firm found that spear-phishing attacks increased 41% over the past year.

    Sources indicate that the tech giant's Phishing Threat Trends Report, Vol. 8 found that overall phishing volume increased 29.8% year over year. Organizations received an average of one dangerous e-mail for every 733 messages, but the bigger concern is how attackers are changing their approach.

    Rather than sending the same fraudulent message to thousands of people, criminals are spending more time researching their targets and creating convincing messages that appear to come from trusted coworkers, businesses, and technology platforms.

    The findings are based on threat data from KnowBe4 Defend, the firm's inbound e-mail security platform, which processes approximately 1.15 billion event signals daily.

    It has been revealed that knowBe4 found that several traditional phishing methods declined significantly compared with 2025. Mobile-focused scams dropped 47.3%, advance-fee fraud fell 31.3%, and missed-message scams declined 11.3%.

    Meanwhile, spear phishing increased 41.1%, pre-attack reconnaissance rose 33.7%, and company impersonation climbed 28%.

    The shift suggests that attackers are finding more value in carefully crafted scams that exploit existing business relationships and workplace routines.

    Recent findings suggest that business e-mail compromise (BEC) remains particularly common, accounting for 51.2% of phishing e-mails analyzed in the report. Human resources, finance departments, and executive leadership are among the most frequently targeted groups.

    Sources indicate that attackers also appear to be timing their campaigns around normal business activity. KnowBe4 found that 90.4% of phishing messages arrive Monday through Friday, with Monday accounting for the largest share at 20.6%.

    One of the report's more troubling findings involves the growing use of legitimate technology platforms to deliver malicious content.

    KnowBe4 found that phishing attacks were twice as likely to originate from legitimate infrastructure in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the previous quarter.

    It has been revealed that that includes AI services, where attackers are taking advantage of trusted domains to host fake developer consoles, login prompts, and credential-stealing pages. The report also identified a 228% increase in AI-brand impersonation attacks between March and August.

    Because these malicious pages can operate on legitimate domains with valid security certificates, users may not see the usual warning signs associated with suspicious websites.

    "For years, security advice has focused on a predictable checklist: Check the sender address, hover over the link, and look for the padlock," said Jack Chapman, senior vice president of threat intelligence at KnowBe4.

    "While still foundational, that guidance is becoming less useful by the day.".

    The findings echo a recent report about management software and AI e-mail assistants. Research from Fortra and Barracuda showed how criminals are using legitimate administrative tools and hidden AI instructions to manipulate owners and compromise systems.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

    According to recent reports, it’s an oft-expressed sentiment, but it’s true: The holidays turn people’s attention toward friends, family, and community. There’s a beauty in the selfless, caring gifts people give to others. And while all that giving feels great, the holidays are also a good time to treat yourself. Plus, it’s getting colder.

    Whether you equate The North Face with everyday city wear or outdoor adventures, it’s a solid, time-tested spot to get a gift for a loved one (or yourself). The brand has jackets and accessories with familiar winter looks, as well as products with less expected silhouettes that still offer protection from the elements in an understated style.

    Here’s a look at some of the best cold-weather gear that will have you wrapping up the gift of warmth and durability… even if that gift is for yourself.

    This is an easy gifting win because the warm, hooded, insulated jacket is a recognizable The North Face staple, evoking an unpretentious spin on the brand’s iconic Nuptse Jacket.

    It’s familiar, but it’s also practical—the kind of gift you feel good about because it’s going to get a ton of use. (And it can withstand the repeated wears.) The attached hood offers protection from biting winds, and the straightforward color options make it easy to pair with a variety of outfits, whether it’s something fun or part of a heavy bundling during the coldest days of winter. This is the perfect type of winter coat: warm but not too puffy.

    The Zaneck Jacket is a great alternative to the Aconcagua, stepping away from the outdoorsy look the brand is best known for. It’s still waterproof and insulated, but it has a longer, more modern cut.

    It has been revealed that the Zaneck comes with a removable faux fur lining for the hood, which, in addition to being warm, means there are a couple of different looks that can be teased out of it. The straight cuffs add to its stylish feel in a way that doesn’t scream “I’m dressed for warmth and not fashion,” even though it’s doing both.

    The Lone Peak Triclimate 2 has a lot in common with the Zaneck. From a distance, they cut a similar silhouette. However, the Lone Peak adds a little versatility if you’re looking for a jacket that can handle a variety of climates.

    Industry observers note that A removable, insulated inner jacket is attached to a removable, insulated top layer, which is fit for rainy conditions or as a spring or fall jacket. The insulated layer converts the whole thing into a winter-ready jacket. It also sports underarm vents capable of releasing heat in the middle of a long hike, ideal for outdoorsy types. The hood is removable and it’s got adjustable cuffs and an adjustable hem, making this a do-it-all jacket.

    It has been revealed that it might be easy to ignore the Pertex Jacket. It’s a bit unassuming. It doesn’t cut as stylish of a figure as the Zaneck, but it’s endlessly useful. The lightweight Pertex fabric will keep you dry in a downpour, but it also offers warmth without marshmallow-like bulk.

    The lightweight aspect makes this the kind of coat you toss in the backseat on the way to a hike, just in case. It’s also great for layering, whether it’s tossed on over a sweater or layered under an overcoat to make a favorite jacket more winter-ready.

    Recent findings suggest that this edition of the classic Base Camp Duffel echoes the design details we love in The North Face’s jackets. While it’s got enough style and a heap of color options for daily use, it’s built for adventure.

    According to recent reports, made with water- and tear-resistant fabric, it boasts 71 liters of storage space, a roomier option to the similar 31-liter version. Like all of the brand’s products, it’s built as if the designers have been through the rigors of outdoor adventures (and they probably have). It’s got a sweeping D-zip opening, backpack straps, mesh pockets, and compression straps in case you’re curious if you can pack 73 liters worth of gear into the 71-liter space. (You know you’ve tried.).

    Sources indicate that the North Face has a lot of hats, none more iconic than this. The Salty Lined Beanie has a classic feel, fitting snuggly over the head with rib-knit texture, a cuffed shape, soft fabric, and ample color options to ensure it will match any jacket or accessory. The Salty Lined Beanie encapsulates the entire The North Face vibe in a small way: It’s stylish enough for a subway ride to work and practical enough for an outdoor adventure. Best of all, it’ll keep your ears warm in either instance.

    Often, the best glove is the one that disappears into the outfit. It looks seamless, keeping hands warm without drawing too much attention. The Etip Recycled Glove is about functionality first and foremost, but the simple design and understated colors makes it look good with a variety of winter outfits.

    While we all like to pretend we aren’t attached to our phones, the Etip makes a great modern gift because its stretchy fleece delivers a snug fit and the palms have touchscreen compatibility. That means you won’t have to take off your gloves to respond to that important text while the snow is falling.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that happy birthday, Hailey Bieber!
    • Of course, the birth-week celebrations have also come with a wardrobe to match.
    • Throughout the years, Bieber has become as known for her style as for her Rhode lipgloss phone cases, playing with understated “quiet luxury,” classic Los Angeles athleisure, and tons of Saint Laurent leather.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that happy birthday, Hailey Bieber! The star has officially turned 30, and to mark another turn around the sun, she kicked off a week of celebrations with a newly introduced navy-blue Rhode drop, a festive campaign, and an intimate video series that followed a week in her life. Throughout the vlogs, we saw the founder in fittings and makeup chairs, spending time with son Jack Blues, and reflecting on the past decade. “Becoming a mom definitely changed me the most in my twenties,” she told the camera. “I always knew I wanted to be a mom, I always knew I wanted kids, and it just totally transforms you as a person for the better.”.

    Of course, the birth-week celebrations have also come with a wardrobe to match. From shearling coats to archival statements, she ushered in the new season with everything from an ivory satin Oriori coat trimmed in gray-white fur to a black silk Armani Privé Fall 2005 set to a Yohji Yamamoto Spring 1998 jacket previously seen on Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy. And we did not expect anything less from the star.

    Throughout the years, Bieber has become as known for her style as for her Rhode lipgloss phone cases, playing with understated “quiet luxury,” classic Los Angeles athleisure, and tons of Saint Laurent leather. As she grew from a teenage model into a business owner and, later, young mother, her taste has evolved over time—but through it all, she has given us some major fashion inspiration.

    So, in honor of her 30th birthday, we rounded up our 30 favorite looks from the star. And between her plethora of Met Gala ensembles, polka-dot prints, and mismatched moments with husband Justin, there was a lot to pick from.

    For the New York Times Dealbook Summit, Bieber takes a page from Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy and wears a Yohji Yamamoto Spring 1998 jacket previously worn by the late It girl.

    Recent findings suggest that bieber wears an iridescent jacket from Matthieu Blazy’s Chanel Fall 2026 collection. With a medley of silver, red, and turquoise mesh, the piece puts an aluminum chainmail twist on the house’s signature tweed.

    For the Academy Museum Gala, Bieber wears a custom bubblegum-pink Chanel dress.

    In a recent development, at the 2026 Vanity Fair Oscar after-party, she hits the carpet wearing a shimmering leopard-print gown, made custom by Armani Privé. She accessorizes with Lorraine Schwartz jewelry and Manolo Blahnik heels.

    While in Tokyo, Bieber wears a textured Issey Miyake egg-carton skirt suit from the Fall/Winter 2000 collection.

    Doing press in Australia, Bieber wears a green Valentino Spring 2026 minidress, with structured shoulders, ruching, and a sweet bow at the hem.

    Bieber attends the GQ Men Of The Year party in a naked dress and sparkly Gucci thong, bringing back the ’90s trend.

    At the 2025 Academy Museum Gala, Bieber steps out in a striking, sculptural gown from Schiaparelli, constructed from brown moiré vintage ribbons for the house’s Spring/Summer 2025 Haute Couture runway.

    Supporting Kylie Jenner at the Kylie Cosmetics anniversary event, Bieber looks to Wiederhoeft for a belted satin midi dress, designed with a chunky belt and thigh-high slit.

    While out for an evening in New York, Bieber turns heads in an electric green minidress from Dolce & Gabbana’s 2003 collection.

    Stepping out in Fresh York, Bieber embraces two of the year's biggest trends—polka dots and capris—all in one go.

    Bieber wears a Marine Serre dress made out of metallic-silver watch straps for a weekend in Miami during the Grand Prix.

    Bieber spends an NYC evening at Cafe Zaffri, wearing a silky ice-blue minidress—a vintage Gucci piece from the fashion house’s Spring/Summer 1998 collection, designed by Tom Ford.

    • According to recent reports, kate Middleton and Prince William have arrived in India for a three-day official visit, their first joint overseas tour since 2022.
    • Sources indicate that the couple will attend the awards ceremony on Tuesday, November 17, when five environmental initiatives will each receive £1 million to expand their work.
    • The royal itinerary extends beyond the ceremony.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, kate Middleton and Prince William have arrived in India for a three-day official visit, their first joint overseas tour since 2022. Unveiled by Kensington Palace over the weekend, the November 16–18 trip is in honor of the sixth annual Earthshot Prize awards in Mumbai. It also marks a significant step in the Princess of Wales’s return to public duties following her 2024 cancer diagnosis.

    Sources indicate that the couple will attend the awards ceremony on Tuesday, November 17, when five environmental initiatives will each receive £1 million to expand their work. Founded by Prince William in 2020, the prize recognizes solutions across five areas, including restoring nature, reducing waste, and addressing climate change. Mumbai is the awards’ first Indian host city, following past editions in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro.

    The royal itinerary extends beyond the ceremony. Kensington Palace said the visit would highlight sustainable urban transportation, responsible manufacturing, youth-led environmental projects, and India’s creative industries. Today, the couple joined cricket great Sachin Tendulkar and local children for a game of street cricket in Ballard Estate, a historic neighborhood in South Mumbai. The Prince and Princess of Wales are also scheduled to attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards, recognizing environmental solutions developed by young people ages 9 to 17.

    The trip is Catherine’s first overseas tour with William since she disclosed her cancer diagnosis in 2024, and her first appearance at an Earthshot ceremony since the Boston awards in 2022. It is also the couple’s second official visit to India, a decade after their April 2016 tour.

    Study: Sign-In Problems Are Primary Drivers of Help Desk Tickets

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (452 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network issues can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a upcoming study from ControlUp.
    • Analyzing 1,069,110 help desk tickets, the IT operations company identified password resets, account lockouts, and multifactor authentication (MFA) issues as major drivers of support demand.
    • In a recent development, at one large enterprise, account-related tickets took a median of 11 minutes to resolve, compared with 50 hours for network problems.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network issues can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a upcoming study from ControlUp.

    Analyzing 1,069,110 help desk tickets, the IT operations company identified password resets, account lockouts, and multifactor authentication (MFA) issues as major drivers of support demand.

    In a recent development, at one large enterprise, account-related tickets took a median of 11 minutes to resolve, compared with 50 hours for network problems. Meanwhile, 87% of network and phone tickets were reassigned between teams, compared with 20% of account tickets.

    Sources indicate that MFA enrollment and re-enrollment problems appeared at 40% of organizations, with one in five linking these issues to employees replacing or upgrading their phones. Virtual desktop problems appeared at 55% of organizations analyzed.

    Traditional phone support remained a major channel for IT assistance.

    Sources indicate that among organizations that recorded how support requests were submitted, 57% reported that phone calls accounted for approximately two-thirds or more of contacts. At one organization, that figure reached 99%.

    Machine-generated tickets from monitoring, security, backup, and patching systems appeared at half of the organizations studied. At 15%, automated tickets represented between 25% and 50% of all requests.

    The research covered enterprises across retail, healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, construction, energy, and IT services.

    ControlUp mentioned the findings highlight the need to evaluate recurring problems and their operational impact rather than relying solely on ticket volume and resolution speed.

    "IT organizations have traditionally measured support performance by how rapidly they close tickets, but that doesn't tell the whole story," said Simon Townsend, senior vice president of marketing and office of the CTO at ControlUp.

    "A password reset that takes a few minutes and an infrastructure failure that disrupts an entire location shouldn't carry the same operational weight.".

    For more information, go to the ControlUp site.

    Microsoft is introducing new tools within its sovereign cloud offerings designed to give organizations tighter control over where their data resides, who can access it, and how critical systems operate, especially in light of AI becoming a bigger part of enterprise infrastructure.

    CoSN, the professional association for K-12 education technology leaders, has released newly introduced guidance to help schools navigate the screen time debate and develop technology policies that protect students while supporting learning.

    AI is changing which human capabilities matter most at work, yet employees are reporting that some of those same capabilities are being eroded, according to a upcoming study from IBM.

    Sources indicate that technology directors touch nearly everything that happens in a school system. Here are three strategies these IT leaders can use to navigate their many duties without losing strategic focus, influence, or sustainability.

    Latest Update: Before & After: Two Best Friends Turned a Stripped-Down Tudor Into a Colorful, Antique-Filled Dream Home

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that anne Hulcher Tollett can’t remember a life without her best friend, Van.
    • The five-bedroom house had good bones and an intuitive flow, but it needed help getting some of its charm back.
    • It has been revealed that “Van’s aesthetic is diametrically opposed to ‘simple’ or ‘builder-grade,’ and although this house had been meticulously renovated and maintained by the previous owners, some of the charm she loves had been removed,” claims Tollett.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that anne Hulcher Tollett can’t remember a life without her best friend, Van. They met in a playpen as toddlers and promptly became an integral part of each other's lives, with many childhood memories taking place in Van’s house growing up. Tollett has been with her best friend through every milestone, including as her maid of honor at her wedding to her husband, Sean, and when the couple put an offer on a suburbanized Tudor home in Richmond, Virginia.

    The five-bedroom house had good bones and an intuitive flow, but it needed help getting some of its charm back. When Van and Sean bought it for their family of four (plus their dog, Jelly Bean, and a small flock of chickens), it was whitewashed and lacked architectural character. In short, it wasn’t up to par with Van’s eclectic style, according to Tollett, but as the principal designer of Hanover Avenue, she reassured her bestie that she could easily take it from suburban chic to warm, layered, and personality-filled without having to completely rework the interior.

    It has been revealed that “Van’s aesthetic is diametrically opposed to ‘simple’ or ‘builder-grade,’ and although this house had been meticulously renovated and maintained by the previous owners, some of the charm she loves had been removed,” claims Tollett. The designer and her team focused on lighter renovations and cosmetic upgrades, walking her best friend through every decision, from wallpaper choices to reworking the staircase to highlight the amazing treasures Van has collected on her travels over the years.

    Throughout the renovation, Tollett and Van leaned into their sisterly shorthand, resulting in a project with very few disruptions. “Our biggest challenge was creating unexpected quirky moments without taking down walls or undoing all of the thoughtful and well-built upgrades that came with the house,” Tollett explains. “We found places on tables, walls, and bookshelves to highlight everything Van and her family have collected over the years. It makes the house feel like theirs and not the product of some design firm.”.

    Walls were covered with grasscloth, patterns were layered on throw pillows and vintage rugs, and anything that wasn’t antique or pre-owned was chosen to add a touch of patina to the space, allowing Van’s collections to truly sing.

    Sources indicate that once Tollett was finished with the renovation, the house told the story of their friendship and a life well lived. Because the designer knows Van like the back of her hand, she was able to create a retreat that feels like a true reflection of who she is and how her family lives without editing out any of Van’s eccentricities. “We understood her design sensibility and took something well-built but fairly plain and made it fun, pretty, and interesting at every turn, which is exactly how anyone would describe Van!” Tollett adds. Besides, who better to design your house than the person who knows you better than yourself?

    FAST FACTSDesigner: Anne Hulcher Tollett of Hanover AvenueLocation: Richmond, VirginiaThe Space: A 4,600-square-foot Tudor home with five bedrooms, four full bathrooms, and two half-baths.

    The barrel back and turquoise chairs were finds that Tollett sourced for Van’s previous home, proving that timeless profiles and accessible sizes can work in many different spaces throughout their lifetimes.

    According to recent reports, “A room like this with a vaulted ceiling and white walls creates a wonderful backdrop for bold pops of color and patterns because it can visually hold its own against furnishings with personality,” she notes. “Van had the beautiful sideboard, and we loved pairing it with the tattooed table.”.

    According to recent reports, possibly one of the most remarkable makeovers in the entire house, Tollett coated the entryway in deep blue paint, topping it off with darling wallpaper on the ceiling for added dimension. “This is a great example of how a can of paint, a roll of wallpaper, and some strategically placed treasures can transform a room,” she says.

    According to recent reports, large-scale grasscloth wallpaper instantly gave the once-all-white box character and rhythm, setting a serene backdrop for the rest of the unique finds in this dining room. The chandelier hanging over the table had long been on Tollett’s list to use in a project, and Van’s home was the perfect spot.

    “The dining room is right near the front door, so it’s hung to look like it's being blown by the entrance breeze—a true classic with a twist!” the designer notes.

    Above the antique bar (whose natural patina plays so well with the wallpaper), are two framed photos of puppets, which Van found during one of her globe-trotting trips. She carried them around in her backpack, and Tollett loved the story behind them so much that she had them framed. On the opposite wall, behind the piano, is a portrait of Van’s grandmother in a vibrant green dress.

    The kitchen was well-maintained when Tollett got her hands on it, but it didn’t feel all that fun, and it needed more than simple cosmetic refreshes like other areas of the home.

    In a recent development, “We removed the major-box island lighting and reworked the storage, hood, and casework on the range wall,” Tollett explains. “We did the same on the wall opposite the range,” she adds, which was in fantastic shape, so they kept it.

    Industry observers note that to give the cook space more character, the designer installed a custom Delftware tile backsplash. The island was also in good shape, so Tollett upgraded the hardware, faucet, face frames, and lighting above it, opting for three Pinch pendant lights which bring an interesting, natural texture to the space.

    “Open concept kitchens are tricky because they are seen from every angle, so we knew we needed to improve the storage to hide clutter,” she adds. Opposite the range wall, Tollett removed the open shelves, creating closed casework instead and topping everything off with pretty hardware and colors that play well with the adjacent dining and living rooms.

    Sources indicate that tollett knew she was going to wrap this powder room in a beautiful butterfly-and-bird wallpaper, so she custom-matched a paint to fully drench the room in a whimsical emerald green hue. They even had their wonderful wallpaper installers cut out a few extra birds and butterflies to extend the design onto the ceiling, creating a more immersive experience. “We wanted the powder room to pack an equal punch to the bold, blue entryway it connects to,” she explains.

    Industry observers note that one of the mantras Tollett and her team at Hanover Avenue follow is “wonderfully weird,” which the hand sculpture extending through the wall to hold the soap perfectly captures. “The space feels not only more fun but also much more personalized to our clients!”.

    During the renovation, Van’s mother passed away, so Tollett transformed this almost-forgotten area into an homage to the matriarch. “We reused her beautiful plate rack and hung all her flawless collections of plates on the walls,” the designer says, officially turning this room, which overlooks the vegetable gardens, into the “plate room.”.

    Sources indicate that they papered the walls in warm neutral grasscloth and hung relaxed Roman shades to softly filter the natural light, furnishing the room with many of the fabulous pieces Van already owned (and loved). “This is a wonderful example of ‘reimagining what you have,’ and finding ways to remember the ones we love in our own rooms,” Tollett adds. “Van’s mom was the coolest!”.

    Recent findings suggest that “Decades of sleepovers in Van’s childhood bedroom allowed me to execute exactly what she was hoping to achieve,” Tollett explains. Though there are many layers of pattern in this sitting area, the designer managed to prevent it from feeling busy by keeping the same serene color palette for most of the textiles, minus a few pops of red for a warm balance.

    “This room is a grown-up translation of Van’s entire design sensibility that began when she was young and was nurtured in her adulthood during her travels,” Tollett adds.

    Recent findings suggest that on the other side of the room is a calming wash of warm white paint and natural textures, giving Van a visual place of rest ideal for sleeping. Tollett calls it a “well-collected, well-traveled, layered space that seems to have evolved all on its own—a sanctuary for Van and Sean,” which makes the designer especially happy since she was the maid of honor at the couple’s wedding.

    In a recent development, the primary bath really only needed some cosmetic upgrades, but they did a lot of heavy lifting. Airy Roman shades soften the space while Van’s mother’s bench and one of her existing rugs give it personality. By opting for two warmer paint colors and swapping out key fixtures, such as the lights, hardware, and faucets, Tollett created a serene, sophisticated escape that looks completely new, all with the same bones.

    Tollett tapped into her childhood memories with her best friend when designing this room. “During slumber parties, Van and I fell asleep across from each other in twin beds, so it felt fitting to create another bedroom that fosters the same kind of childhood chatter,” she claims, adding that stepping inside is like stepping into a time machine going back to 1983.

    According to recent reports, along with the beds, much of the look was directly inspired by Van’s childhood bedroom, the round green pillow on the bed having been plucked directly from it. The pre-existing Tudor windows were perfect for the vintage vibe.

    Sources indicate that tucked away at the far end of the home is a spot connected to the sunroom lounge. Dubbed the “dayroom”—an informal spot dedicated to relaxation and reading—Tollett wanted it to feel cozy and as collected as the rest of the home but still a bit private. They washed the walls in a soft gray-green hue and did the same to the custom day bed, finishing off the room with antique bookcases in a complementary gray tone. It’s easy for small rooms like these to feel overcrowded, but the pale color palette takes away some visual weight.

    As founder and principal designer of Hanover Avenue, Anne Hulcher Tollett is intimately involved in every project the Richmond-based design firm takes on, from high-end residential to boutique commercial. Tollett finds a thrill in uncovering her clients’ design styles and endless joy in creating their dream homes that reflect who they are.

    Enterprise AI Spending Outpaces Adoption Growth, Report Finds

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (720 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.
    • The venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025.
    • A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

    The venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025. The share of enterprises paying for AI rose from 55% to 65%.

    A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.

    Industry observers note that menlo's methodology describes revenue figures as annualized run rates. The $176.8 billion estimate therefore should not be read as $176.8 billion already spent during the first nine months of 2026.

    In a recent development, the report also distinguishes unusually heavy spenders from the typical respondent. Average reported spending reached 4.7 times the prior year's level, while the median reached 2.2 times. That gap suggests a smaller group of large spenders drove the average substantially.

    Recent findings suggest that the practical implication is that an industry growth figure may be a poor benchmark for an individual organization's budget. Buyers need to understand their own workload growth and the results it produces.

    "Agents are changing the economics of software," Menlo principal Derek Xiao remarked in the firm's announcement.

    Industry observers note that menlo reports that agents account for 80% of tokens on OpenRouter, a service providing access to multiple models. That measures activity on one platform, rather than all enterprise AI use. Token consumption also measures processing volume, rather than completed business outcomes.

    An agent that makes repeated attempts can consume more resources without delivering proportionately more value. For procurement teams, the relevant comparison is consequently the cost of completing acceptable work, including the review it requires.

    According to recent reports, menlo estimates that Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google capture 69% of enterprise AI deployment spending. That measure is distinct from their shares of enterprise language-model API spending, a narrower category. The figures should not be used interchangeably.

    The report draws on a Morning Consult survey of nearly 400 U.S. enterprise decision-makers responsible for more than $4 billion in AI spending. Market totals are modeled estimates informed by surveys, public filings, and third-party reports. Menlo discloses investments in Anthropic and OpenRouter.

    In a recent development, A separate announcement from Information Services Group describes buyers putting more emphasis on the economics and reliability of production deployments. ISG claims ongoing security and observability work remains necessary as organizations scale.

    Industry observers note that that provides a useful distinction between market demand and business value. Suppliers can generate growing revenue while customers still determine which deployments justify the cost.

    Industry observers note that for enterprise leaders, the new spending estimate strengthens the case for examining usage beyond license counts. It leaves the harder purchasing question with the customer: How much worthwhile work did the increased spending actually buy?

    Menlo's State of Enterprise AI report is available here.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One day, you’re listening to The Cheetah Girls soundtrack on the way to school with an armful of Silly Bandz and the next, you’re worried about making rent, hours lost to Google Sheets, and an unexpected medical bill when you still have a $52 request floating in a sea of Venmo transactions.
    • Recent findings suggest that as for the world we’ve grown into?
    • Recent findings suggest that “As more of our everyday experiences are shaped by technology and algorithms, people are finding value in things that feel more personal, creative, and unexpected.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Let’s face it: Growing up is hard. One day, you’re listening to The Cheetah Girls soundtrack on the way to school with an armful of Silly Bandz and the next, you’re worried about making rent, hours lost to Google Sheets, and an unexpected medical bill when you still have a $52 request floating in a sea of Venmo transactions.

    Recent findings suggest that as for the world we’ve grown into? Nearly two years into Trump’s second presidential term, with AI raising questions about how much of our thinking we’ll hand over to machines, adult life can feel relentlessly optimized and not as chic or shiny as we imagined it as kids. But even if the future feels uncertain, we continue to hope. 2026 has revived the desire to make room for the colorful, playful, and wonderfully impractical again, and that impulse has a name: whimsy.

    Recent findings suggest that “As more of our everyday experiences are shaped by technology and algorithms, people are finding value in things that feel more personal, creative, and unexpected. Inspiration is still incredibly crucial, but so is the freedom to take what you see and make it your own,” Sydney Stanback, global trends and insights lead at Pinterest, tells Cosmopolitan.

    Recent findings suggest that “People are craving more imagination and fun in their everyday lives. There is a real appetite for aesthetics that feel less polished and predictable and more personal, and whimsy gives people room to try something they might not have considered before.”.

    And the numbers don’t lie. Pinterest searches for “bedazzling patterns” have increased by a whopping 9,187 percent this year, while “bedazzled phone case” searches are up 8,012 percent. Even “whimsical office outfits” have jumped 885 percent.

    From Kylie Jenner’s bejeweled birthday cake and “princess kitty”–themed fete to the deconstructed silhouettes and glittery garments taking over spring/summer 2027 runways, we’re all finding increasingly creative ways to inject personality into our days. In an increasingly automated world, doing things simply because we can is the ultimate act of rebellion. At its core, whimsy is about making magic out of the mundane, whether we’re revisiting childhood obsessions now that we (sort of) have adult money or taking the DIY approach to life to make it more vibrant.

    That’s why Cosmopolitan invited 18 colorful, charismatic, and unapologetically authentic tastemakers to share how they’re romanticizing life and embracing their eccentricities. Because to be whimsical is to be human!

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When Tiffany Howell of Night Palm Interiors designs a home, her vision transcends conventional norms, veering into an ethereal realm—an approach she calls “the poetry of place.” In Howell’s mind, film, fashion, and music are as essential as decorative art, and she uses these inspirations to create theatrical spaces that ignite all the senses—layering texture, sound, scent, light, and form to evoke deep emotion. When executed with this level of intention, a room becomes an environment you don't merely look at but fundamentally feel.

    According to recent reports, when Miele partnered with Howell to create a dream kitchen for an installation at Art Basel, she seized the opportunity to reimagine what a kitchen can be. The result is the interactive 360-degree rendering seen here—a wildly imaginative digital environment that inspired the brand’s upcoming physical installation at Miami’s premier art fair. “I wanted an undeniable sexiness, a beautiful, sensory experience,” she claims. “I created the space with characters in mind that I’d invite to a dinner party in this kitchen.” After all, the kitchen is a home’s heartbeat, an interactive space with multiple purposes.

    “I do think the kitchen is really one of the most tender rooms in the house,” Howell indicates. She leaned into that romance by installing black cabinetry with blossoming branches and birds in iridescent greens and pinks. The cabinets are an homage to her love of 1920s chinoiserie furniture and fashion, seen through a very glamorous, Los Angeles lens. That California focus also meant bringing the outdoors in. The grand conservatory space harnesses diffused, natural light with the promise of the scent of jasmine wafting into the room. Howell’s ideal playlist sets the tone with jazz greats and ambient synth-pop.

    Recent findings suggest that “I wanted to create a kitchen that’s a completely sensory experience,” Howell explains. “The sound of a crackling warm fireplace, the aroma of a meal cooked for loved ones, or of making coffee in the morning.” For Howell, these aren't incidental details; they are the sensory architecture that turns raw space into lived emotion. In Howell’s view, this kitchen is “also a place where you can take a nap, read a book, or write in your journal. Every moment in this room can become a ritualistic experience of living well.”.

    Recent findings suggest that when it came to the practical needs of a kitchen, Howell used Miele as a muse, an invitation to eschew the pale minimalism so common in luxury kitchens. “The appliances are so elegant, they kind of act as the jewelry of the room,” she says. “And their functionality and ease of operation give you back time to live better, relax with a drink, hang out with family and friends, and create the stories that make up a life.”.

    Consider the Miele Built-In Coffee System and wine cooler in matching dark finishes which are nearly camouflaged so the technology reads more as furniture than appliance. That tension between heirloom design and high-tech styling becomes a unified part of a lived-in, well-collected home. Accent pieces, including a vintage Fortuny pendant lamp over the kitchen island, and upholstered chairs in the conservatory with detailing reminiscent of antique lingerie, create a moody environment well suited to Miele's black-finished lines that resemble rich obsidian.

    Industry observers note that the 36” Full Surface Induction Cooktop features a frameless, flush design that disappears into a dark-veined countertop. Transforming the entire glass surface into one expansive cooking area, it fits up to six pots or pans at once and with Intelligent Pan Recognition and SmartSelect White controls seamlessly transfer power settings wherever pans are moved. On the same wall is the 30” Handleless Combi-Steam Oven XXL, with DualSteam technology that emanates ASMR sounds of steam cooking, and a black glass façade that resembles a framed panel or window. From the cool, flush glide of the induction cooktop to the whisper-quiet hum of precision steam, the technology engages the senses rather than interrupting them, turning modern convenience into an intuitive, tactile ritual. Rather than breaking up the wall with a stack of conspicuous appliances, these seamless integrations keep the architecture artful. And for added convenience, Miele’s elegant touch controls are enhanced with Wi-Fi connectivity for an easier user experience.

    Recent findings suggest that howell’s concealment of technology is exhibited in her use of the 42” French Door Refrigerator with its elongated custom handles and a dark lacquered paneled front that echoes the floral chinoiserie motifs—an unconventional solution that turns a mundane appliance into a piece of decorative art. Once the refrigerator doors are open, the Brilliant Light Pro illumination makes it easy to survey the food inside the large capacity interior.

    Sources indicate that “How do you nurture yourself and others in the kitchen?” Howell asks. Her answer: a design that creates a restorative space evoking intimacy and slowness, where technology can encourage a lightness and give us back more time. By composing every sight, surface, scent, and sound into a single harmonious narrative, Howell proves that a kitchen shouldn't just be an aesthetic statement—it should be something you feel in your bones. “What excites me is building a new world with more possibilities,” Howell says. “I don’t think I could design any other way.”.

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.
    • According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.
    • The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.

    According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.

    The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.

    The Redmond-based firm recognized approximately 129 million malicious messages spoofing the sender domains of tracked business services during Q3.

    DocuSign was the most frequently spoofed brand in September, accounting for 29% of the month's tracked spoofing activity. Adobe, SurveyMonkey, and Barracuda also experienced increases toward the end of the quarter.

    The research found that some malicious messages were delivered despite failing e-mail authentication checks and being identified as threats.

    In September, tenant- or user-level security overrides applied to 63% of these messages with a recorded security outcome — most involved tenant-level exceptions.

    Microsoft warned that overly broad exceptions intended to support legitimate business communications can weaken protection against impersonation attacks.

    The firm emphasized that these findings do not establish whether recipients opened the messages or whether accounts were compromised.

    Microsoft also recorded approximately 141,000 malicious Teams call attempts during Q3.

    According to recent reports, attackers increasingly used ordinary personal names instead of explicitly impersonating IT support personnel. Such display names accounted for 46% of an observed sample in July, rising to 88% in September.

    Meanwhile, QR code phishing declined 67% compared to Q2, totaling roughly 12.1 million attacks.

    CAPTCHA-gated phishing activity increased toward the end of the quarter, reaching 3.1 million detected attacks in September. SVG attachments played a significant role in the increase.

    Credential theft remained the primary objective of malicious attachment campaigns, with approximately 94% to 96% of payload-based attacks directing owners to phishing sites or fraudulent sign-in pages.

    Microsoft recommended reviewing Exchange Online Protection and Defender for Office 365 configurations, enabling Safe Links and Safe Attachments, and strengthening authentication protections.

    The organization also advised organizations to review security exceptions and verify the identities of external Teams contacts before responding to suspicious requests.

    For more information, go to the Microsoft blog post.

    Microsoft is introducing upcoming tools within its sovereign cloud offerings designed to give organizations tighter control over where their data resides, who can access it, and how critical systems operate, especially in light of AI becoming a bigger part of enterprise infrastructure.

    AI is changing which human capabilities matter most at work, yet employees are reporting that some of those same capabilities are being eroded, according to a new study from IBM.

    #100707. Tech Report: What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1018 w)
    📖 Baca
    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, in vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor.
    • Gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp.
    • It has been revealed that venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, in vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor. Both share a passion for keeping priceless and nearly century-old vehicles in use on the open road rather than displaying them under glass. But some see the drive itself as challenge enough, while stalwarts adhere to what’s called the road book. This is a hundred or so pages of complex navigational directions that the copilot uses to navigate instead of a map, maintaining a constant flow of instructions to the driver. It is this book and how closely you follow it that decides the eventual winner.

    Gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp. In early September, I climbed into the copilot seat of his 1939 Aston Martin C-Type Speed Model Roadster Bertelli—just one of two ever built, with an experimental aerodynamic body that earned it the nickname “the Flying Pea”—and stayed there as he drove six hundred kilometers of “left at the traffic lights, right at the cow” for the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run. The rally started in Venice and ended, after a scenic but challenging detour high into the Dolomite mountains, at Monza, the home of Italian Formula 1, just in time for practice day of the Grand Prix.

    It has been revealed that venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets. But the city was chosen this year because it was also the end point of the last LV rally of its kind: the La Serenissima Run from Monte Carlo to Venice in 2012. Gianandrea won that one as copilot, with his father, Giuseppe, at the wheel. The pair also won the one before it—the Boheme across Hungary, the Czech Republic, and Austria—in 2006. This time, however, the pressure was on me too.

    I have been a copilot before, and I can tell you it’s no picnic. Rally racing in vintage cars is less about speed and more about timing. It’s an exercise that requires pinpoint accuracy at the time-stamp points in the overall course and, most critically, in the regularities. These are fiendishly short time-over-distance sections in which crossing the line just a few hundredths of a second late—or early—earns strict penalties. Sensibly, the day before the race began, Gianandrea took me out in the Aston in the Veneto countryside to practice, especially those critical regularities.

    I could have opted for an easy life. The rally allowed competing cars, dating from 1931 to 1969, to use the road book or follow the course using a map in a dedicated phone app. But where’s the fun in that?

    Recent findings suggest that “If you join a competition, you follow the regulations and strive to do your best,” Gianandrea notes. “As an Italian, if you paint numbers on the door of my car, I will want to win.”.

    Every car in a rally like this comes with its own idiosyncrasies. On flat ground, someone driving a souped-up 2026 sports car would find these tests difficult to nail. In the reality of race conditions, the regularities often involve steep climbs or descents and unexpected corners, alling for an expert hand at the wheel—and foot on the gas pedal. The tendency of some car doors to swing open at hard bends (ours has the “suicide” doors with hinges on the back instead of the front, beloved by early carmakers) only adds to the excitement. The purpose of driver and copilot is to battle and overcome all the mechanical and computational challenges—and get our ride to the finish line bang on time.

    It has been revealed that louis Vuitton has been involved in these glamorous and exacting vintage rallies since 1993. The Dolomites Run represents an enthusiastic return to the genre after a fourteen-year gap and, perhaps tellingly, the organization’s global sponsorship (since 2025) of Formula 1. Unconfirmed rumors circulated in the field that the choice of ending the rally at a Grand Prix could well be repeated—and soon—in other countries in the future.

    Industry observers note that it’s easy, after all, to see why a fusion of style and cars with six- and seven-figure price tags might appeal to Louis Vuitton and competitors alike. Not surprisingly, at every coffee and lunch stop, the LV effect sprinkled the race with an added sense of luxury. In between, our snaking caravan carried the glamour of a century of motoring along with it. At every hairpin you got a glimpse of a gull-wing Mercedes, a 1931 Bugatti two-seater (my personal fave), and a shimmering behemoth of a Bentley in quick succession. These cars would turn heads anywhere. But in Italy, arguably the home of the sports car, they brought smiles, applause, and gasps in even the tiniest village that passed by in our slipstream. I swear I even saw a nun with a glint in her eye at one set of traffic lights.

    Industry observers note that navigating, I was promptly learning, is not so much about providing a constant babble of information as it is knowing how to give clear and simple instructions—and only when strictly needed. As the finish neared in Monza at the end of two long days on the road, I was able to give Gianandrea the most helpful instruction of all: “Nothing for 15 kilometers.”.

    “That,” he very kindly replied, “is the mark of a pro.”.

    Even after the engines cooled, we were still clueless about how well we’d done overall. That changed at the final event, a dinner inside the Sforzesco Castle in Milan. Gianandrea stepped up, beaming, as winner of the race, and for the first time as driver. I stood somewhat sheepishly behind him as copilot as he received the trophy from Pietro Beccari, CEO of both Louis Vuitton and Louis Vuitton Fashion Group. It was an impressive swirl of Murano glass created by Venini, housed in its own equally impressive traveling case, made (naturellement) at Louis Vuitton’s atelier in Asnières.

    Gianandrea has promised me visiting rights.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Pictured above: A holiday-ready space by designer Marie Flanigan.
    • Christmas is just around the corner, and as the holiday spirit makes its way into our homes, it’s a good time to give your seasonal decor a refresh.
    • However, if you’re in the mood to try something a little different, here are seven trends on our radar for a chic Christmas.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Pictured above: A holiday-ready space by designer Marie Flanigan.

    Christmas is just around the corner, and as the holiday spirit makes its way into our homes, it’s a good time to give your seasonal decor a refresh. This year, on-trend doesn’t have to mean brand-new—designers love decorating with heirloom pieces collected over time.

    However, if you’re in the mood to try something a little different, here are seven trends on our radar for a chic Christmas.

    According to recent reports, this winter, our decor is taking a note from European culture—again. Swedish folk art is emerging as a hot winter trend in both holiday and home decor. Defined by bold red hues, tulip motifs, and S-scrolls, the style blends cozy-core with the heritage style craze.

    It has been revealed that “European folk influences are so massive right now,” states designer Johanna Lyle of Jo Lyle & Co. “Think Swedish Dala horses, quilt motifs, and decorative stitching. I think we will see those continue into holiday decor.”.

    It has been revealed that when it comes to her tree decor, interior designer Francesca Grace waves a hand at the carefully contrived, and she’s not alone. “My ornaments are collected from my travels, so the tree is really a collection of memories. I love unpacking them and remembering where each one came from. They don’t all match, and I wouldn’t want them to,” notes Grace. “I let the ornaments lead. That mix feels much more personal to me, and it gives the tree something new to say as the collection grows.” This year’s trends hinge on antiqued, inherited style, with one-off pieces that channel bold character and hardly ever come with a matching set.

    Interior designer Marie Flanigan likes to add a fresh twist to her seasonal decor with dried oranges and pops of cranberry red.

    It has been revealed that “We've seen such a beautiful resurgence of dried citrus in holiday decorating over the past few years,” Flanigan explains. “And I think cranberries are ready for their moment to shine. Their rich red hue feels especially festive, and I love the idea of incorporating them into fresh greenery, draping them across a mantel, or pairing them with dried oranges for a more layered look.”.

    It has been revealed that if there’s one classic Christmas element Grace hopes makes a comeback, it's multicolored lights. Inherently nostalgic, these bold-hued bulbs were a ’90s staple.

    In a recent development, “I’m ready for a little less restraint on the tree. Those reds, blues, greens, and yellows immediately bring back the feeling of Christmas as a child. They also pull together a collection of ornaments that might otherwise seem completely unrelated. White lights can be beautiful, but I want my Christmas tree to have some mischief,” says Grace.

    It has been revealed that the classic red-and-green combination may take the title for the most iconic holiday palette, but this year, color trends are going complementary. While base colors stay warm and slightly rusted, patterned pieces are taking on cooler tones. This year, we’re also trading traditional plaid for Scottish tartan.

    “Warm crimsons, rich browns, tactile fabrics, and blue-green plaids make a beautiful holiday palette,” notes Elizabeth Bennett, cofounder of the interior design firm Kobel + Co.

    In a total rejection of mass-manufactured everything, handmade felt pieces are taking holiday homes by storm. The style has even coined a new holiday aesthetic: #Kitschmas, and, according to Lyle, it’s here to stay. “As AI continues to homogenize design, things made by humans will feel more special and important. Handmade and crafted items create stories around decor that feel meaningful and can be treasured year after year,” she says.

    Moody browns are steadily emerging as the new neutral as we inch closer to the new year, and lucky for our winter design schemes, the hue really is as versatile as it seems. Paired with powdery blues, bold crimsons, and even minty greens, chocolate brown grounds nearly any palette and matches every metallic hue.

    “I’m particularly drawn to chocolate brown as an unexpected foundation for holiday color palettes. It's incredibly rich and versatile. I love the idea of moving beyond traditional red and green and allowing the existing colors of a room to inform the holiday decor. You can create something incredibly festive through tonal layering, subtle metallic accents, and variations in material,” Flanigan explains.

Filmed at some of the era’s most impressive estates, the series serves up grand ballrooms, château-style manors, and sumptuous drapery in abundance. It’s enough to stir up a little real estate envy. Fortunately, three extraordinary Gilded Age homes are currently on the market, offering the chance to live out that fantasy in real life. Take a peek inside below.

Located along the Connecticut border with New York, the star of the 268-acre compound is an eight-bedroom mansion designed by architecture firm Hunt & Hunt that spans more than 15,000 square feet. Featuring elaborate millwork, moldings, plasterwork, and stained glass, the manor features plenty of amenities. Olympic-sized indoor pool? Check. Elevator? There are two. Grounds? They include formal gardens, four guest houses, a private lake, and even a hedge maze. The opulent spread is listed with Leslie McElwreath of Sotheby’s International Realty.

    Recent findings suggest that an Anglo-Italianate brownstone in New York’s Chelsea Historic District, the Van Ness House was built in the mid-19th century and was later enlarged to its present 7,800-square-foot size. Revamped by ELLE Decor A-List designer Miles Redd, the seven-level landmark pays homage to its elegant roots, with preserved plaster moldings, custom millwork, elegant wallcoverings, and heated oak floors in a retro chevron pattern. In the back, a landscaped private garden is paved in limestone and dotted with linden trees that turn golden in the fall. Atop the five-bedroom townhouse, which is listed with Nick Gavin and Amber Gregory of Compass, is a rooftop garden with views of Saint Peter’s Church.

    Recent findings suggest that spanning 14,100 square feet, this Beaux-Arts mansion right off Fifth Avenue was constructed in 1902 by architect James R. Turner and William G. Killian. Its interiors, meanwhile, are by John Russell Pope, the genius behind the Jefferson Memorial and the National Gallery of Art. Clad in a medley of brick, limestone, and marble, the eight-bedroom house has retained its stately proportions throughout the years, including a formal dining room lined in carved wood panels. Also inside are a trio of staircases, an elevator servicing six of the seven floors, and two rooftop terraces. It’s listed for $35 million with Brian Meier and Amanda Barba of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices.

    Sources indicate that geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

    Recent findings suggest that A lot of us commiserate about commuting into the office, but there are a few positives to seeing your coworkers regularly, like finding your fellow movie buffs to discuss the latest films with, or bonding with the colleagues you grab drinks with after work. Another upside? Your group may do white elephant gift exchanges, Secret Santa, or at the very least, have an office holiday party. If you are doing a present swap this season, finding creative, affordable gifts for your coworkers could be tricky.

    First, there’s determining the budget; then it’s figuring out whether to get them something practical, fun, edible, or just plain silly. Our thoughtful recommendation is to get a gift they can use immediately or leave at work, like a cute tissue box cover, hand warmers (because the office is always cold), or even a small diffuser that makes the air around them smell better. We found 35 such items they’ll love, and if they truly want to, they could bring and use them at home too.

    According to recent reports, the best gifts for coworkers are the ones they didn’t know they needed until they actually have the item in their hands—and can’t ever part with it. “Rechargeable hand warmers are a sleeper hit when I give them as gifts around the holidays,” states Managing Editor Sarah Esgro. “People always come back and thank me again because they didn’t realize how much they needed them.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, prince Harry has been back in the UK for some weeks now, and he’s wasted no time in letting everyone know about it, with plenty of public moments including a surprise appearance on This Morning and a family outing to London's Winter Wonderland. But while fans of the Duke of Sussex celebrate his return, the Palace is remarked to be “infuriated” with his recent engagements and, in particular, his request to join the “grid.”.

    Speaking to The Express, royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams accused Harry and Meghan Markle of purposely timing their public appointments to take attention away from other members of the royal family.

    Recent findings suggest that “We must assume this has been deliberate. This is deplorable,” the royal expert stated, adding, “[The Palace is] indeed right to be infuriated.”.

    But while Fitzwilliams accuses Harry of intentionally scheduling his engagements to outshine his royal counterparts, perhaps it's all just bad timing—which is where the royal “grid” comes into things...

    Sources indicate that the royal “grid” is a meticulously organized schedule of the royal family’s engagements and appointments. Although the actual “grid” is not available to the public, fans of the royal family can keep up with their plans via the official website. According to the site, official royal engagements are published up to eight weeks in advance.

    It has been revealed that according to The Express, Prince Harry has requested that he be added to the royal “grid.” His motive for the move hasn’t been confirmed, but there are of course plenty of theories. Some critics, like royal commentator Fitzwilliams, believe that Harry wants to intentionally create more scheduling conflicts with the other royals. Others take the more agreeable stance that the duke simply wants to avoid any further calendar clashes.

    One insider, for example, noted that Harry is “mindful” of his fellow royals and their looks, and tries his best to avoid overlapping with them. “He knows about those things and he is obviously mindful of that as he’s planning his own activities as well,” the source told The Times.

    The royal family is split into various households, with Clarence House taking care of King Charles and Queen Camilla and Kensington Palace looking after the Wales family, for example. These households are made up of large teams, covering everything from catering to housekeeping. Also in the royal household are those who plan and manage the family members’ calendars—these are overseen by private secretaries and diary coordinators.

    A previous advertisement for such a job at Kensington Palace remarked, “The role will be responsible for managing the seamless delivery of multiple complex diaries to ensure the smooth and effective coordination of engagements and events.”.

    As for what the role involved? “Compiling and managing coordinated diary updates and weekly overviews; providing regular briefings; communicating diary changes to all key stakeholders, both internally and externally; and carrying out follow-up actions as necessary, as well as ensuring that all events and engagements are accurately recorded,” the listing explained.

    Sources indicate that “The successful candidate will have a proven ability to manage complex diaries and will have excellent communication skills,” the vacancy ad went on. Being a team player and having a proactive mindset were just some of the other requirements of the role, in addition to maintaining confidentiality and discretion, which the listing described as “paramount.”.

    The pair have already soft debuted on Instagram Stories—and by that I mean Adrian posted a photo of Julianne holding his dog, which she went ahead and shared to her own account. Oh, and Adrian was at Disney night!

    Meanwhile, back in September Julianne told E!, "I might not be single,” before cryptically adding “There's a lot to discuss off-camera.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the professional dancer also told the outlet that when it comes to dating post-divorce from Brooks Laich, “It's all energy-based. I don't really have a type. It's more connection, and that's it. I've been very intentional about what I'm putting out and what I'm excited to attract and hopefully be attractive to, but I will say that I kind of just threw that out the window. It brought me back to the joyful, playful side, versus being so serious. Sometimes, when you're intentional, you can get a little bit tunnel vision, and so, I kind of was like, 'You know what? I'm just gonna be playful and fun.’”.
